papers.title: COMPARISON OF THE CORROSION PROPERTIES OF CoCrMo DENTAL ALLOYS IN ARTIFICIAL SALIVA
papers.abstract: CoCrMo alloys are known for their biocompatible properties, which, together with their favorable mechanical properties, mean they can be efficiently used in dentistry. With the development of selective laser melting for the fabrication of 3D printed objects, interest in the corrosion properties of this alloy has risen in the field of prosthodontics. In the study, CoCrMoW dental alloys were studied in artificial saliva at body temperature i.e. 37 °C. Different forms of CoCrMoW alloy were selected: a reference sample, i.e. original material as-received from the supplier, a casted sample acquired from an ordinary procedure in a dental laboratory, and two 3D printed samples made from CoCrMoW powder using the selective laser melting method (SLM). Electrochemical, spectroscopic and hardness measurements were conducted. It was shown that the reference and cast samples have similar microstructural and electrochemical properties, while the electrochemical properties of the 3D printed samples differ, most probably due to the effect of the higher micro porosity and chemical composition of the alloys.

papers.title: Microstructure characteristics and surface oxidation behaviour of SLM WC/IN718 composite
papers.abstract: In this work, WC/Inconel 718 composite was fabricated by selective laser melting (SLM) the IN718 superalloy powders decorated with surface embedded WC powders. Also, the composite was heat-treated by a designed double-aging regime for microstructure tuning. The resulting microstructure and surface oxidation behaviour of the as-printed and the heat-treated composites were studied. The results revealed that the homogeneous microstructure was obtained, and the obvious weld beads structure with fine dendrites was detected on the surface in the SLM composite. After the double-aging heat treatment, the matrix showed a confined growth from 21.81 to 26.14 μm and the weld bead structure disappeared. XRD and EBSD analysis confirmed the formation of γ, γ′, γ′′, WC, (Nb,M)C, δ and Laves phase in the composites before and after heat-treatment. The high-density GND accommodated the strain incompatibility and the internal residual stress in different constituents. Furthermore, the underlying mechanism of oxidation behaviour was discussed.

papers.title: Density Analysis of Additive Manufactured Metal Parts Using Laser Ultrasonics
papers.abstract: Selective laser melting (SLM) technology can be used to rapidly form metal parts of any structure, but the structural properties of the manufactured parts are different from those of traditional metal parts. This paper investigates the ultrasonic characteristics of the Additive Manufactured metal parts produced by Selective Laser Melting (SLM) technology and studies the relation between the metal density and the longitudinal wave velocity in different forming directions. An experiment has been carried out by using a pulsed laser to induce ultrasonic waves in additive manufactured 316L stainless steel parts. The experimental results show that the longitudinal wave velocity in different forming directions is strongly correlated with the metal density. The samples with higher densities have more similar velocity in different forming directions, and hence are more isotropic. The relation between the metal density and the ultrasound velocity has been found by fitting the experimental data into a quadratic curve. The results of this work can be potentially used for evaluating the density of the additive manufactured metals and hence evaluating the physical properties by measuring its ultrasound velocity.

papers.title: Assessment of the Effects of Si Addition to a New TiMoZrTa System.
papers.abstract: Ti-based alloys are widely used in medical applications. When implant devices are used to reconstruct disordered bone, prevent bone resorption and enhance good bone remodeling, the Young's modulus of implants should be close to that of the bone. To satisfy this requirement, many titanium alloys with different biocompatible elements (Zr, Ta, Mo, Si etc.) interact well with adjacent bone tissues, promoting an adequate osseointegration. Four new different alloys were obtained and investigated regarding their microstructure, mechanical, chemical and biological behavior (in vitro and in vivo evaluation), as follows: Ti20Mo7Zr15Ta, Ti20Mo7Zr15Ta0.5Si, Ti20Mo7Zr15Ta0.75Si and Ti20Mo7Zr15TaSi. 60 days after implantation, both in control and experimental rabbits, at the level of implantation gap and into the periimplant area were found the mesenchymal stem cells which differentiate into osteoblasts, then osteocytes and osteoclasts which are involved in the new bone synthesis and remodeling, the periimplant fibrous capsule being continued by newly spongy bone tissue, showing a good osseointegration of alloys. A 3-(4,5-dimethylthiazol-2-yl)-2,5-diphenyltetrazolium bromide (MTT) assay confirmed the in vitro cytocompatibility of the prepared alloys.

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of silicon addition on Young's modulus and osseointegration of TiMoZrTa alloys for biomedical implants.
summary_en.method: Four TiMoZrTa alloys with varying Si content were prepared and characterized for microstructure, mechanical properties, and biological response.
summary_en.result: All alloys exhibited good osseointegration and cytocompatibility, with no adverse effect from Si addition.
summary_en.validation: In vitro MTT assay and in vivo rabbit implantation model confirmed biocompatibility and bone integration.
